Summarize how a REDCap field is related to project metadata

Source: R/field_relationship_summary.R
field_relationship_summary.Rd

Identifies upstream references and downstream uses of one REDCap field using a codebook's metadata. Helps reviewers explore project structure and locate configuration to inspect before changing a field.

Usage

field_relationship_summary(
  field,
  codebook,
  include_diagnostics = FALSE,
  include_inspection_log = FALSE
)

Arguments

field

One exact dictionary field name, including checkbox parent names.

codebook

A codebook returned by build_codebook().

include_diagnostics

Include project-wide interpretation issues as an additional diagnostics tibble (Project Diagnostics). Default is FALSE.

include_inspection_log

Include every inspected metadata location and reference diagnostic as an additional inspection_log tibble. Default is FALSE. This is independent of include_diagnostics.

Value

A list with classes redcap_field_relationship_summary and list, containing seven tibbles by default:

  • field: the selected field's definition and context.

  • upstream: fields it references, directly or indirectly.

  • downstream: fields and project settings that reference it, directly or indirectly.

  • references: related reference occurrences with original expressions.

  • summary: explanations grouped by metadata location, expression, and reference interpretation.

  • issues: interpretation issues in selected or related metadata.

  • coverage: project-wide source counts, interpretation limits, and exclusions.

Optional tibbles are diagnostics (project-wide interpretation issues, when include_diagnostics = TRUE) and inspection_log (the full inspection inventory, when include_inspection_log = TRUE).

Details

A codebook supplies field definitions, expressions, and event/repeat context needed to interpret references. Build it once to explore several fields without repeated API calls. Record data is not needed. Older codebooks without complete definitions must be rebuilt.

Use dictionary field names rather than labels or exported checkbox columns. For example, supply symptoms, not symptoms___fever.

Reading relationships

Upstream means what the selected field references; downstream means where it is referenced. Each related item appears once, with its minimum depth and one representative shortest reference chain. Alternative related references remain in references.

references has one row per occurrence; summary groups occurrences, so their row counts can differ. Chains describe field-level connections, not continuous paths through particular events or repeating instances.

Interpreting references

relationship identifies the connection type, while field_matched records whether the referenced field exists in the dictionary. resolution describes syntax and qualifier interpretation, not data quality.

status_note appears as Interpretation note in the viewer. It explains unresolved, context-dependent, or unclassified references. A blank note means no interpretation limit was detected; it does not validate the configuration. Notes apply to individual occurrences in references, grouped evidence in summary, and the displayed chain in upstream and downstream. In issues and diagnostics, they explain issues at metadata locations.

Known field references remain linked when qualifiers need interpretation. Unknown fields and unsupported annotation candidates do not create traversable links; their evidence remains available in interpretation issues.

Checkbox references

The report includes whole-checkbox and individual-option references. reference_choice and reference_choice_label identify the referenced option. choice_code identifies the containing choice label when an expression occurs in a choice label; it is not the referenced option.

Inspection scope

Inspected sources include branching logic, calculations, supported field annotations, piping, embedding, and the custom record label. The report does not evaluate expressions, predict changes to stored values, or establish referential integrity. Configuration outside the inspected metadata, such as alerts and external scripts, may contain additional uses.

coverage and optional diagnostics describe the entire project and are identical for every field using the same codebook. issues retains details relevant to the selected field and related items. The optional flags control returned detail, not analysis or API calls.

See also

build_codebook(), view_field_relationship_summary(), save_field_relationship_summary()

Examples

relationships <- field_relationship_summary("weight_kg", mock_codebook)
relationships
#> <REDCap field relationships>
#> Field: weight_kg (follow_up)
#> Upstream: 1 item
#> Downstream: 6 direct items, 1 indirect item
#> Reference occurrences across returned chains: 12
#> Action-tag condition: 1; Calculation: 1; Piping: 4; Field embedding: 1; Default value: 3; Unknown relationship type: 1; Branching logic: 1
#> Interpretation issues: 3 related metadata locations (see issues).
#> Project Coverage: project-wide metadata inspection; see coverage for sources and exclusions.
#> Indirect connections are reference chains, not predictions of value or behavior changes.
#> Project interpretation limits are summarized in coverage.
relationships$summary
